name: IC-7100
subtitle: Field reference
kicker: Independent reference. Not an Icom publication and not affiliated with Icom.
verified: Compiled from the Icom IC-7100 Basic Manual (A7085H-1EX-6) and Service Manual (S-15008XZ-C1). Figures and band plans are for the USA version; other versions differ.
specs: HF, 6 m, 2 m and 70 cm. USA models have no 4 m band
USB, LSB, CW, RTTY, AM, FM, DV. WFM receive only
Two SO-239. ANT1 is HF and 6 m below 74.8 MHz, ANT2 is 2 m and 70 cm above it
13.8 V DC plus or minus 15 per cent, negative ground. 22 A or more
0.9 A standby, 1.2 A at full audio
30 A on the DC cable. Two 5 A spares supplied
Plus or minus 0.5 ppm, 5 minutes after power on
Triple superheterodyne, double conversion for WFM
0.15 microvolt on HF with P.AMP1, 0.11 microvolt on 144 and 430
0.18 microvolt on 144 and 430 at 12 dB SINAD
More than 70 dB on HF, 6 m and 70 cm, more than 65 dB on 144 and 430
More than 2 W into 8 ohms at 10 per cent distortion
Plus or minus 9.99 kHz in 10 Hz steps
None. AH-4 or AH-740 on the tuner socket, or an AT-180 on ACC
USB does CI-V with no converter. The remote jack needs a CT-17
keys: Push on, hold about a second for off. Rotate for volume. Turn the DC supply on first.
Cycles the touch key rows M-1 to M-3. It is not a settings tree.
Opens the quick menu. Push again to close.
Selects memories, or drives passband and offset when those are active.
One window for mic gain and transmit power.
Keyer speed about 6 to 48 wpm, and CW pitch about 300 to 900 Hz.
Push announces frequency, mode and meter. Hold about a second to lock the dial.
Listens on the transmit frequency in split.
Clarifier on or off. Shift with the M-CH knob, plus or minus 9.99 kHz.
External tuner on HF and 50 MHz, or the call channel on 144 and 430.
In CW, zero beats the received signal.
D-STAR repeater mode on or off.
Recalls memo pads, newest first. Hold to write one.
The receiver conditioning keys, as printed.
Back out with MENU or the return arrow on screen.
quick: All modes. Split, VFO swap and memory write live here.
DUP, AGC, TONE, DSQL, VOICE, KEYER, DEC, COMP, RTTY, CS, TBW
Varies by mode. Repeater shift and tone, AGC, the keyer and compressor.
MEMO, SCOPE, SWR, DTMF, VOX, BK-IN
Varies by mode. Break-in, the band scope and the SWR graph.
SCAN, SKIP, VOICE, CS, CD, MW, DSQL, DTMF, VOX
The touch rows in D-STAR DR mode.
tasks: Set frequency and mode, pick the channel with M-CH, then the memory write key in the first touch row.
V/M in the first touch row. The M-CH knob steps channels.
The scan key in the first touch row. Hold UP or DN 1 second to start.
The split key in the first touch row. XFC listens on the transmit frequency.
The mic and power key, then adjust with the dial.
In FM, the shift and tone keys in the second touch row. One-touch repeater holds DUP.
SET then My Station then My Call Sign, once. Register with a gateway repeater.
control: The remote jack on the rear through a CT-17, or over USB with no converter
Auto, or 300 up to 19200. Write yours below
CS-7100 software to clone, RS-BA1 for remote control
trouble: Antenna connected, correct socket for the band, and inside a band edge
Wrong antenna socket. ANT1 is HF and 6 m, ANT2 is 2 m and 70 cm
Mic gain too high. Set it watching the ALC zone
There is none. Use MENU or the return arrow on screen
It needs 22 A. Size the supply and use short, heavy DC leads
notes: No internal tuner, despite the size of it. Whatever you put up has to be resonant or matched by something you carried in.
Two antenna sockets, split at 74.8 MHz, and the wrong one is the first thing to check when a band seems dead.
There is no EXIT key. If you are used to an IC-7300 you will hunt for it.
Twenty-two amps on HF. Size the supply for that even if you never run it.
The detachable head is a connector, and connectors fail. Carry the spare control cable.
The main unit runs hot. Keep the MB-62 bracket clear of the vents and nothing on top.
settings: CI-V address, as read from set mode
